item.title: Cardi B Joins GTA Festival
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Travis Scott and Cardi B joined GTA VI's Miami launch festival as Rockstar set November ticket lottery deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Scott and Cardi B will bring GTA VI’s music to Miami on November 21 for a two-stage festival at Mana Wynwood, two days after the game’s launch.

Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black and SoFaygo share the Cactus Jack Presents bill. Metro Boomin joins them, while Justice will play a DJ set. Rockstar Games has teamed with PlayStation and the crew behind III Points for the show.

For Scott and Cardi, the link starts with new songs made for the game. His track “RHYNO” and her song “Don’t Chart” are part of Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album. Both tracks are out now.

The 34-track set is due November 19, the same day as the game. Fans will have two days to hear it before the show.

Justice brings a second strand of the game’s sound to the bill. The French duo wrote the score, which shifts with how each player moves through the game.

Their own score album is due December 11, with 30 tracks plus digital bonus songs. Rockstar Games released this launch trailer on October 15, 2026.

The game’s radio hosts bring more of Miami’s roots to its world. Trick Daddy and Trina helm Dirty South Classics, which plays rap from across the South. They made the pairing public on October 8. Vice City is the game’s take on Miami, set within the wider state of Leonida.

Kodak has a place in that world, too. He confirmed he appears in the game after fans saw his likeness in a new set of images. Rockstar shared them on November 5.

His face tattoos and 1800 Block chain helped fans spot him, though details of the role are still under wraps.

Fans who want to see the live show must enter a draw by November 10 at 4 P.M. ET. They will draw names at 7 P.M. ET. Winners can buy up to two tickets the next day at noon ET.

The show is for guests 17 and up.

item.title: Zamaera and Samad Savage Bet on Themselves With Hard-Hitting Single “Xperience”
item.dc:creator: Brxton Lee
item.description: Zamaera and Samad Savage turn ambition, pressure and hard-earned resilience into “Xperience,” an explosive trap collaboration connecting Malaysian and American hip-hop.
item.content:encoded:
Every rapper has a motto. Few of them come with a warning label.

“You’re losing a hundred percent of the shots you don’t take, so when you take it better not miss.” That’s the bar at the center of “Xperience,” the new single from Malaysian independent star Zamaera and American rapper-producer Samad Savage. Half of it is motivation. The other half is a threat.

The track dropped Friday, November 6, 2026, on Mean Malaya Entertainment. It’s the second time these two have linked up, and this one goes straight for the throat.

Savage made the beat himself, and he didn’t make it pretty. It’s aggressive, high-energy trap that sets the tone before anyone says a word. Zamaera goes first, and she doesn’t open with a flex. She opens with a panic attack. She wakes up from a bad dream with her future looking nothing like she pictured, sweating and holding on to the only things she controls: her mind and her breath.

From there it’s a crash course in what ambition costs. She cuts the wasted time, then cuts the people, and admits the ones she dropped were the closest to her. She calls the road a marathon. Then she drops a bar that belongs on every young artist’s wall: “If you live by praise then you’ll die by the diss.” Everybody raps about blocking out the haters. Not many admit the cheering can take you out too.

Savage answers with a perfect mirror. She woke from a bad dream; he wakes up “from a good nap,” because sleeping on the competition is what he does best. He brings the jokes and the flexes, from eight-pack energy to an A$AP Mob shoutout. The realest part is his backstory. As a kid, rapping was his only escape from “the loneliest place,” so every win now goes right in your face.

The hook is where it all clicks. It runs from having no experience to visions of millions and a house in the Carbon Canyons, then lands on the title’s double meaning: living what everybody else only wants to experience. The pre-chorus keeps it simple. They came from the bottom, broke more times than they can count, and survived. Under pressure, diamonds shine.

The connection goes back to 2023 and “Kill My Vibe,” a track the two built without ever being in the same room. For a couple of years that’s how it stayed: two artists on opposite sides of the world, trading ideas across time zones.

In 2025 they finally met face to face, and they got straight to work. “Xperience” started from nothing in New York City. It went through version after version, and it wasn’t finished until 2026, when they shared a stage at SXSW in Austin, Texas. They took the energy from that show back into the song and closed it out.

Three years from the first collab to this one. In an era of songs made in an afternoon and forgotten in a week, that kind of patience says a lot.

If anybody has earned the right to rap about betting on yourself, it’s Zamaera. She’s a rapper, singer and songwriter who mixes hip-hop with electronic sounds, and she’s done it all independently. She even built her own label, Mean Malaya Entertainment, to push Malaysian talent and connect it with creative scenes around the world.

Her 2026 has been big. At SXSW she created the Made in Malaysia stage and brought five Malaysian acts to Austin, and the showcase is already locked in to return in 2027. In August she showed up on “So Much To Say” from TroyBoi’s FT EP. That led to stage time with him at Breakaway Festival in Charlotte, Global Dance Festival in Denver, Brownies & Lemonade in Los Angeles and EDC Korea 2026.

Then came September. Zamaera performed at Rick Ross’s Rap Arena in Miami, and she was the only international artist on the lineup. A Malaysian indie rapper on a Rick Ross stage, repping her country by herself. Moments like that don’t happen by accident. She went and got it.

Samad Savage brings the same energy from the other side of the world. The American rapper and producer has built his whole career himself. He makes the beats, writes the verses and keeps full control of the vision. His music deals with real life, resilience and saying exactly what he means.

You can trace that through his catalogue, from The Grey Area to Trust the Weird Kids to Duo-Litty. On “Xperience” he handles the beat and a verse, then passes the mic back to Zamaera, and the song circles back to her opening lines. When the guy telling you to control your future also built the beat you’re hearing, you believe him.

Hip-hop has always belonged to people who refused to wait their turn. Today that crowd includes a rapper from Malaysia who builds her own stages and a producer from the States who builds his own beats. They don’t share a city or a scene. What they share is a work ethic.

“Xperience” is what you get when two people like that meet halfway around the world and decide to say it plainly. Take the shot, and don’t miss.

“Xperience” by Zamaera and Samad Savage is out now on all digital streaming and download platforms worldwide via Mean Malaya Entertainment.

item.title: Coolio Comes Back To Life In Dheezy’s Space-Themed Video
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Coolio joins Dheezy on screen through archival footage as the Australian rapper rolls out a collaboration years in the making.
item.content:encoded:
Coolio is coming back to life onscreen through a collaboration with Australian rapper Dheezy built from previously unreleased footage.

Dheezy’s team says it worked closely with the late rapper’s estate to assemble the “Shoot For The Moon” video.

The production combines archival green-screen footage with new performances inside a space-themed setting. M-Strange produced the song, which closes Dheezy Does It LP after four years of sessions between Australia and Los Angeles.

“Dheezy Does It LP is more than an album—it’s the culmination of years of hard work, sacrifice, and a lifelong love for Hip-Hop,” Dheezy told AllHipHop in a statement.

The album also includes contributions from the late rappers Nate Dogg, Proof and Chino XL.

For Coolio’s appearance, the production team matched camera angles and lighting before building the surroundings with 3D effects. Those steps allowed footage recorded during his lifetime to share the screen with Dheezy’s performance.

Snoop Dogg, Kurupt, E-40 and Planet Asia appear elsewhere on the album alongside Onyx and Big Twins.

Dheezy’s team describes Eminem as his biggest musical influence, with several guests connected to the Detroit rapper’s circle.

“This project brings together artists and influences that helped shape my journey, and I’m proud to finally share it with the world,” Dheezy said. Those connections were already taking shape before he brought this album together.

Dheezy teamed with Bizarre for the six-track Killah Kombo EP in 2023, with Kuniva and Swifty McVay also involved.

That project included “Flip Em All The Bird,” bringing his D12 collaborations into an earlier music video. That earlier EP also included Obie Trice and production from K.E. on the Track.

Coolio died in September 2022 at 59, but recordings he made during his lifetime have continued reaching listeners. The posthumous “A Star Is Born” with Treach and DJ Wino followed in 2023, adding another collaboration to his catalog.

His career stretched from “Fantastic Voyage” to “C U When U Get There,” with “Gangsta’s Paradise” becoming his biggest crossover hit. The Dheezy video gives another archived performance a place in a new release.

KXNG Crooked executive-produced Dheezy Does It LP, which opens with an introduction from Eminem.

item.title: Brandy Embraces Her Success In Personal EBONY Power 100 Speech
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Brandy makes room for her own pride as Coco Jones salutes her at EBONY’s gala following a year of memoir revelations.
item.content:encoded:
Brandy brought her struggle with self-image into the spotlight while accepting one of EBONY’s biggest honors. The singer discussed learning to appreciate her accomplishments during the Power 100 gala on November 9.

Coco Jones introduced Brandy at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles and sang a tribute built around her music. Brandy used her turn at the microphone to discuss grief, growing up under pressure and the experiences behind her memoir, Phases.

“Tonight I can feel the weight of what I’ve accomplished without making myself feel smaller,” Brandy said. Her remarks put a personal struggle alongside the career achievements being celebrated in the room.

That subject has followed Brandy for a year as she tells her own story beyond the stage. Phases arrived in March, covering her childhood, early fame and the work of finding her own voice outside other people’s expectations.

An earlier Jennifer Hudson Show interview about the memoir offers context for that conversation. Monday’s ceremony gave Brandy another opportunity to address those experiences while accepting recognition from her peers.

The honor also follows her hometown celebration in Mississippi this summer, when she received keys to McComb and Pike County. She pledged $100,000 for new middle school band instruments during that visit.

Brandy shared this year’s special honoree court with Flau’jae Johnson, Keith Lee, Lena Waithe, Byron Allen and Victor Glover.

Tisha Campbell hosted the ceremony, which also recognized leaders working across music, business, sports and their communities. The event also marked more than 80 years of EBONY’s history.

“Celebrating the Black leaders moving our culture forward is central to EBONY’s mission, and last night was a true reflection of that mission,” EBONY CEO Eden Bridgeman said in a statement. “We are honored to have such an influential class of individuals in one room to share their stories and celebrate such incredible achievements.”

The musical performances ranged from Kirk Franklin’s opening appearance to Tyrese’s run-through of his catalog. Monica also joined the program to introduce Bridgeman’s closing speech before the evening wrapped.

T.I. finished his set with “Pistol on the Dance Floor,” delivering its final verse a cappella.

item.title: Denzel Washington Turns Thief In "The Take"
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Denzel Washington's "The Take" brings Robert Pattinson and Daisy Edgar-Jones into a Manhattan bank-heist thriller.
item.content:encoded:
Denzel Washington plays a convincing thief, leaving fans doing double takes after Netflix dropped the first look at “The Take.”

The movie casts him as Christian Carter, a master thief with his sights on Manhattan’s richest bank.

Carter brings Noah, played by Robert Pattinson, into his crew. The former Army captain is still finding his feet after leaving the service. But Noah’s girlfriend, Rose (Daisy Edgar-Jones), also works as a teller at the bank. Noah must work out who to trust to survive the robbery.

The story skips back and forth in time and mostly sticks to Noah’s view. “You only know what he knows,” director Fernando Meirelles told Netflix’s Tudum.

On set, Washington would change his lines as they filmed. “Each take is a surprise,” Meirelles said.

Edgar-Jones’ take on Rose changed the director’s view. “I see what I have and I incorporate it,” he said.

Playing a thief flips Washington’s role in “Inside Man.”

In Spike Lee’s 2006 bank-heist film, Washington played Detective Keith Frazier. Clive Owen played the man Frazier faced: Dalton Russell, who led the robbery at a Manhattan bank.

Netflix bought the script for “The Take” from Simon Kinberg in May 2020, years before it named the stars. Five years later, on May 14, 2025, Netflix named its three stars: Washington, Pattinson and Edgar-Jones. It was still called “Here Comes The Flood.”

Meirelles would direct Kinberg’s script and serve as a producer. Kinberg and Audrey Chon were also set to produce through Genre Films, with Samson Mucke as executive producer.

The cameras started rolling on November 3, 2025, and the shoot ended on January 22, 2026. The shoot took the team to Jersey City, Hoboken and Newark in New Jersey, as well as Atlanta and New York City.

Its release plans had shifted along the way. On January 7, 2026, while the shoot was still underway, Netflix included the film in its plans for releases that year.

By November 4, the new title and a 2027 release plan were known. The first look pins down the date: January 15, 2027, in select theaters and on Netflix.

item.title: Nick Cannon Says Eminem Crossed The Line With Mariah Carey
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nick Cannon revisits the insults that pushed him to defend Mariah Carey and explains his part in the Eminem battle.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Cannon wasn’t letting Eminem take shots at Mariah Carey without putting himself in the line of fire.

The Wild ‘N Out creator is revisiting why he stepped into a feud that started before he married Carey. During his conversation with Maury Povich on On Par, Cannon explained that Eminem’s comments about his then-wife made the dispute his business, too.

“He disrespected my woman, man. You can’t come at my wife and don’t expect to get this work,” Cannon told Povich.

That answer came when Povich brought up the long-running clash between the two entertainers. Cannon’s account focused on his marriage rather than who delivered the better diss record or drew a bigger online reaction.

Cannon said the tension between Carey and Eminem was already there when he entered the picture. He described their earlier connection as professional and said Eminem had presented it differently.

“Yeah. I mean, I think he he and Mariah had a professional relationship. Uh, which he professed to be a personal relationship. Uh, and so that was way before me,” Cannon said.

“So then by the time we got married, he had some some harsh words because I guess he was still in his feelings,” Cannon told Povich.

His explanation put a personal reason behind a feud that eventually spilled into several records. Cannon wasn’t only defending his own name when he answered Eminem, according to his account of the dispute.

The two traded attacks again in 2019 after Cannon discussed Eminem on T.I.’s ExpediTIously podcast. Eminem later took aim at Cannon on Fat Joe’s “Lord Above,” and Cannon responded with “The Invitation.”

Cannon then released “Pray For Him” with The Black Squad, keeping the exchange going through another recording. Eminem also responded on Twitter during that round of the dispute, bringing Cannon’s collaborators into a fight rooted in his former marriage.

“The Invitation” also included Suge Knight alongside Hitman Holla, Charlie Clips and Prince Eazy. Those appearances brought more voices into the exchange, while Cannon’s latest interview returns to why he says he got involved.

item.title: Westside Gunn Makes Peace With WWE After Nick Khan Meeting
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Westside Gunn reconnects with WWE’s Nick Khan as his 4th Rope wrestling event and new HEELMATIC album arrive this week.
item.content:encoded:
Westside Gunn is putting his WWE fallout behind him after a meeting with Nick Khan opened the door to a fresh start. The Buffalo rapper credited WWE’s president with resolving their issues in a Tuesday announcement that paired the company with his own 4th Rope brand.

Westside Gunn wrote on X, “S/O to NICK KHAN 4 MAKING EVERYTHING RIGHT, WHATEVER HAPPENED IN THIS PAST DOESN’T MATTER…..WERE HERE TO PUSH THE CULTURE FOWARD.” He tagged both wrestling companies and shared four photos with the message.

He didn’t announce contract terms or spell out what the two companies will do together. There’s no named wrestler joining WWE or new television arrangement in his post, which centers on his meeting and the relationship going forward.

That’s a change from the frustration he aired in November 2025. Westside Gunn said then that he’d been removed from a WWE Raw show in Buffalo after buying a $5,000 seat, and he vowed to stop promoting the company.

His public break with WWE also involved complaints about wrestling references in his music and artwork. He said the company had threatened action over those uses after years of him buying tickets and celebrating its performers.

Westside Gunn kept building 4th Rope while the dispute played out publicly. The promotion has brought together live wrestling, Hip-Hop performances and clothing, with talent including The Hardys and Zilla Fatu appearing at its events. He first announced the venture in 2022 and introduced Parker Boudreaux as its first official wrestler after the former WWE NXT performer appeared for AEW.

The timing puts his reconciliation in the middle of another busy week for that business. He’s bringing 4th Rope and Mass Appeal’s Heels Have Eyes: Heelmatic event to New York’s Melrose Ballroom on Thursday, November 12, with tickets already sold out.

He’s also using the event to play music from HEELMATIC, his 16-track album arriving Friday through Griselda Records and Mass Appeal. The rollout follows last year’s Heels Have Eyes trilogy and keeps his wrestling interests tied directly to his records.

Thursday’s event will stream live on the REVOLT and 4th Rope YouTube channels.

item.title: Juice WRLD’s Mom Confronts Music Industry’s Cost Of Chasing A Dream
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Juice WRLD’s mother backs new research showing young music workers face mounting money worries and mental health struggles.
item.content:encoded:
Juice WRLD’s mother is putting hard numbers behind the money problems and anxiety facing young people trying to build music careers. Carmela Wallace’s Live Free 999 foundation backed new MusiCares research showing most young respondents cannot comfortably pay their bills through music.

The findings, released Tuesday, examined 203 music professionals ages 18 to 24 in MusiCares’ broader 2026 Wellness in Music Survey. Among that younger group, 79% reported difficulty covering expenses through music work and nearly 69% earned $25,000 or less in total annual income.

“Jarad was my son before he was Juice WRLD, and I know firsthand how important it is to recognize when someone is struggling and help them get the care they need,” Wallace said. “His music helped so many young people feel less alone.”

“I started Live Free 999 because I wanted to make sure those young people, and the next generation of artists, have somewhere to turn for support,” Wallace continued. “We partnered with MusiCares because we wanted to understand what young music professionals and music professionals are experiencing today and not make assumptions about what they need.”

“The more we know, the more we can do to help before someone reaches a crisis,” Wallace added. The findings also showed 52% of young respondents experienced moderate to severe anxiety on a typical day.

The survey put money worries alongside the emotional pressures of entering the business. Housing, basic necessities and health care ranked among respondents’ biggest financial concerns, while finding appropriate providers and stigma remained barriers to getting help.

Wallace established Live Free 999 after losing her son in 2019 and has continued expanding its mental health work. The foundation now partners with Music Health Alliance on $1,000 grants that help emerging artists cover therapy costs.

MusiCares’ broader survey gathered responses from more than 3,300 people across the music industry. The younger participants’ responses provide a specific look at those still trying to establish themselves rather than a measure of every musician’s experience.

Live Free 999 also supports a paid Bring Change to Mind fellowship that lets high school students help shape mental health resources.

item.title: Singer-Songwriter ADOM: From BOSTON to Latin Dance, Bringing a Hip-Hop Influence to “Ella Tiene el Cuerpo”
item.dc:creator: Brxton Lee
item.description: Former BOSTON songwriter ADOM takes a sharp turn into Latin pop, earning UK chart placements with his independent single “Ella Tiene el Cuerpo.”
item.content:encoded:
The former BOSTON songwriter’s independent Latin-pop single reached two UK charts, highlighting an unexpected musical evolution.

A songwriter with three original compositions on a BOSTON album might not be the first name that comes to mind when you think of Latin dance music. But ADOM, formerly known as Anton Cosmo, has spent his post-rock career moving between genres, and his single “Ella Tiene el Cuerpo (She’s Got the Body)” offers one of the clearest examples of that evolution.

Released December 5, 2025, through ChromaWave Records, the track combines Latin-pop energy with a hip-hop-influenced rhythmic foundation. Tight percussion, a low-end groove and a dance-oriented hook position the record in territory far removed from the guitar-driven sound that first introduced ADOM to a national audience.

The experiment also produced a measurable result.

“Ella Tiene el Cuerpo” reached No. 28 on the UK Official Singles Downloads Chart and No. 43 on the Official Singles Sales Chart, spending one week on each ranking. The placements, documented by the Official Charts Company, marked a UK chart appearance for an independently released track that crossed the stylistic boundaries of ADOM’s earlier work.

While the recording is rooted in Latin pop rather than traditional rap, its rhythmic approach reflects the increasingly fluid relationship between dance music, pop production and hip-hop. The track is less concerned with fitting neatly into one category than with finding a groove that connects them.

ADOM wrote, produced, performed and mixed the recording, with engineering assistance from Phil Greene, whose credits include New Kids on the Block. Grammy-winning mastering engineer Adam Ayan handled the final master. The production credits are significant because the artist making the stylistic transition was also responsible for building much of the sound himself.

That degree of creative involvement is not new.

Recording as Anthony Cosmo, ADOM was a guitarist and songwriter with BOSTON, contributing three original compositions to the band’s 2002 album Corporate America: “Stare Out Your Window,” “Turn It Off” and “Cryin’.”

In a Guitar World interview, BOSTON founder Tom Scholz confirmed the unusual songwriting arrangement, explaining that Anthony had written three of the album’s tracks.

For a musician coming out of a band so closely identified with a particular sound, the decision to embrace Latin dance and contemporary rhythmic production represents more than a cosmetic change.

ADOM has spoken about the difficulty of being defined by an earlier chapter of his career.

“I’m definitely not the same person I was when I was touring with BOSTON. Why would the music be the same?” he told Neon Music.

That perspective runs through “Ella Tiene el Cuerpo.” Rather than revisiting the arena-rock arrangements of his past, ADOM emphasizes rhythm, electronic textures, and a hook designed for dance-oriented listening.

The song’s additional treatments, including an Eden Arcade mix and a slowed-down version, further explore how the same composition can function in different listening environments.

The release also arrives during a broader creative transition. ADOM’s current project, House of Memories, connects twelve original songs with twelve short films, presenting each release as a separate chapter within a larger narrative.

The series began with “THE UNKNOWN” in October 2026, with “Don’t You Cry” scheduled for November 20.

For ADOM, the distance between BOSTON’s Corporate America and a Latin-pop single appearing on the UK charts illustrates the changing possibilities available to an independent artist who writes and produces his own material.

“Ella Tiene el Cuerpo” may not be a conventional hip-hop release, but its rhythmic influences and crossover sensibility make it part of a larger conversation about where pop, Latin music and hip-hop intersect.

And for a songwriter whose career began in classic rock, that intersection represents another direction worth exploring.

Listen to ADOM: Spotify | Official Website

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Damon Dash Gets Seven Days To Hand Over Roc-A-Fella Archives
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Damon Dash faces a seven-day deadline to surrender Roc-A-Fella archives as a judge approves his $550,000 life-rights sale.
item.content:encoded:
Damon Dash has seven days to surrender his Roc-A-Fella archives after a bankruptcy court approved his $550,000 life-rights sale.

The handover includes footage, photographs, memorabilia and materials tied to the unreleased project known as “The Roc-A-Fella Movie.”

The order filed November 10 requires Dash to deliver physical originals and digital files, including available metadata. He must also provide access information for relevant online archives and identify anyone else holding those materials.

The court ordered Dash to “not destroy, conceal, alter, transfer, encumber, or otherwise dispose of any Archival Materials.” The sale package describes video content believed to exceed 100 hours, alongside scripts, recordings and other film materials.

Everlasting Films won the October 1 auction with its $550,000 offer, beating Doug Peters’ $500,000 backup bid.

Attorney Christopher Brown, whose financial participation AllHipHop previously reported, helped fund the winning offer, although Everlasting remains the sole purchaser.

Dash did win protection against having his future swept into the deal. The sale covers his life through September 4, 2025, when he filed for bankruptcy, leaving later experiences, newly authored work and earnings from later services outside its reach.

The court also drew a line around what Dash must personally share. “Nothing in this Order requires the Debtor to disclose, record, narrate, or otherwise communicate to the Purchaser any memories, experiences, or thoughts that were not recorded, transcribed, or otherwise expressed as of the Petition Date.”

That protection doesn’t stop the buyer from portraying his earlier life using archives, public records or other lawfully obtained information. Dash also cannot interfere with the ownership or exercise of the rights transferred under the order.

Approval still leaves payment and closing ahead, with Everlasting required to complete both within ten days after entry. If that deadline passes without closing, the trustee can proceed with Peters’ backup offer without another court order.

The trustee is also investigating a previously undisclosed potential literary contract and pending book that could bring additional rights into the sale.
